query: For high-entropy alloys intended as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components, what single intervention could improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the expected outcome compared with current intermediate-layer performance, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing of high-entropy alloys to create a optimized microstructure with a grain size of 100 nm and a precipitate density of 10^18 m^-3 will improve heat-transfer capability by 20% while preserving structural integrity under temperature and loading conditions of 500°C and 100 MPa.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a random solid-solution microstructure
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing with a temperature of 800°C, a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, and a processing time of 2 hours
generation.mechanism: Enhanced thermal conductivity due to optimized microstructure and improved mechanical properties due to precipitate strengthening
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in heat-transfer capability may vary depending on the specific high-entropy alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with tailored thermo-mechanical processing and characterization of microstructure and thermal conductivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured thermal conductivity is not within 10% of the predicted value, the hypothesis is falsified
